filename: Perspectives on Systematic Cloud Microphysics Scheme Development With Machine Learning.pdf
title: Perspectives on Systematic Cloud Microphysics Scheme Development With Machine Learning
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: Cloud microphysics (bulk process rates, hydrometeor size distribution representations, and ice/liquid microphysical processes)
testbed_rationale: This is a commentary/perspectives review article and does not introduce or provide a newly curated or standardized simulation/observational dataset.
pain_points: Lack of first-principles governing equations for cloud microphysics creates both structural and parametric uncertainty.
Observations (satellites and in situ) generally capture instantaneous states rather than microphysical process rates directly.
Equifinality in top-down constraints where multiple parameter combinations match macroscopic emergent observables.
Offline training of ML parameterizations often fails or becomes unstable when coupled online due to multi-timestep compounding errors and forward Euler assumptions.
Discontinuity and numerical limiters (e.g., minimum/maximum thresholds) in traditional schemes are difficult for continuous ML models to capture.
Scale dependence and spatiotemporal resolution mismatches between microphysical interactions (< 1 km) and coarse ESM grid boxes (~50-100 km).
Code and hardware portability issues between Fortran-based CPU ESMs and Python/GPU deep learning libraries.
extraction_notes: The paper is a perspective/review commentary synthesizing challenges, paradigms, and ML approaches for cloud microphysics scheme development. The Data Availability Statement explicitly confirms that no new data was generated or used.
